who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), lane impls (V15) under proofs-1113
where: blaze-vm, cargovm2.sh with a new VM_LANE (impls)
what: The first cargo test -p hir-ty-lean in a new VM lane took 23 min 17 s (load average 880 on blaze-vm while it ran); the brief said several minutes.
cost: about 25 minutes of a lane waiting on one compile
cause: a new VM lane gets its own target directory, so the whole dependency graph of hir-ty-lean is built from nothing on a VM shared by many lanes
whys: one target per lane keeps lanes apart; nothing shares compiled dependencies between lane targets; the VM is oversubscribed by parallel lanes
class: per-lane cold builds on a shared VM cost each lane the whole graph
prevention: not done: seed a new lane target from a warm one (a copy, or a shared read-only dependency cache) before its first run
workaround: start the first build of a lane before reading the code
